rv.q: Like a classic folk ballad, full of understated outrage and exquisite down-home music, “Coal Country,” in an encore presentation at the Cherry Lane, tells the devastating true story of the 2010 explosion at the Upper Big Branch coal mine of West Virginia, which killed 29 miners, and exposed the criminally negligent conduct of the mine’s owner.
This heartbreaking tale of corporate malfeasance in America’s heartland still deserves to be seen.
No fictional tragedy can compare to the devastation of reliving a true one.
Coal Country’s excellent ensemble hits the motherlode over and over, mining it for its every ounce of unbearable grief, labor unity, and moral outrage.
It is profound and memorable in scope and power.
But Earle's soulful, folk-inspired mountain music transforms a good play into a great one.

cn.t: Critics praise this heartbreaking documentary drama about the 2010 West Virginia mine disaster for its understated power and Steve Earle's soulful folk music, calling it riveting theater that effectively memorializes tragedy.
